verdict.rationale: Pulumi describes itself as an open source platform, and its documented DIY backend lets users store state in object storage they manage instead of using the hosted Pulumi Cloud. The pricing page says 'Self-hosting available', but a community report citing the docs says self-hosting of the full platform is only offered in the Enterprise Edition, and another user says they could not build airgapped infrastructure, so self-hosting the complete product is gated and its extent is unproven. Missing for 10: documented self-hosting of the full Pulumi Cloud service on non-enterprise tiers, setup and deployment docs for self-hosted Pulumi Cloud, and hands-on corroboration of offline/airgapped self-hosted operation.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can self-host the core product

citations.quote: Pulumi is an open source platform for building, deploying, and managing cloud infrastructure using your favorite programming languages.
DIY backend: a “Do It Yourself” backend that stores state in an object store you manage—AWS S3, Azure Blob Storage, Google Cloud Storage
